open_points.subject: service API listener in an owner-only start
open_points.text: Registry serves each surface on a listener of its own, at its configured address, and decides nothing about reachability beyond that listener's own form — bound exclusively, an IPv6 one for IPv6 alone (A17 rule 1).
open_points.question: Does an owner-only start omit the service API listener and its address, as A17 requires, or must Registry always serve both surfaces on configured listeners?
options: An owner-only start serves only the owner interface and opens no service API listener.
Registry always serves both surfaces, so a service API address and listener are required even without service tokens.
open_points.default_guess: Treat the owner-only mode in A17 as an explicit exception and open only the owner-interface listener.

witness.initial: The owner-interface address and all other required owner settings are present, while all four service tokens and the service-API address are absent.
events: The owner starts Registry with that configuration.
Registry checks whether the configuration is valid and decides which listeners to open.
outcomes: Under A17, Registry starts in owner-only mode, opens only the owner-interface listener and serves no service API.

Under the State 3 preamble, Registry serves each of its two surfaces on its own configured listener; the missing service-API address either prevents startup or must be supplied and its listener opened.
witness.observer: The owner or host administrator sees whether Registry starts and whether a service-API listener exists.
